pr.title: Mark unions non-const-propagatable in `KnownPanicsLint` without calling layout
pr.description:
Fixes #123710

The ICE occurs during the layout calculation of the union `InvalidTag` in #123710 because the following assert fails:https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/5fe8b697e729b6eb64841a3905e57da1b47f4ca3/compiler/rustc_abi/src/layout.rs#L289-L292

The layout calculation is invoked by `KnownPanicsLint` when it is trying to figure out which locals it can const prop. Since `KnownPanicsLint` is never actually going to const props unions thanks to PR https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/121628 there's no point calling layout to check if it can. So in this fix I skip the call to layout and just mark the local non-const propagatable if it is a union.
pr.author: gurry

issues.title: ICE: assertion `left == right` failed: `non-Aggregate field with matching ABI but differing alignment`
issues.body:
### Code (reduced) ```Rust #[repr(packed)] #[repr(u32)] enum E { A, B, C, } fn main() { union InvalidTag { int: u32, e: E, } let _invalid_tag = InvalidTag { int: 4 }; } ```

Regression test for #93688. union InvalidTag { int: u32, e: E, } let _invalid_tag = [unsafe { InvalidTag { int: 4 }.e }]; // An enum without variants. Regression test for #94073. union NoVariants { int: u32, empty: Empty, } let _enum_without_variants = [unsafe { NoVariants { int: 0 }.empty }]; // A non-UTF-8 string slice. Regression test for #75763 and #78520. struct Str; let _non_utf8_str: Str::<{ unsafe { std::mem::transmute::<&[u8], &str>(&[0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5]) } }>; } struct S4(u8,[u8; 3]); #[repr(packed)] #[allow(dead_code)] struct S5(u8,u32); pub fn main() { unsafe { let s4 = S4(1, [2,3,4]); let transd : [u8; 4] = mem::transmute(s4); assert_eq!(transd, [1, 2, 3, 4]); let s5 = S5(1, 0xff_00_00_ff); let transd : [u8; 5] = mem::transmute(s5); // Don't worry about endianness, the u32 is palindromic. assert_eq!(transd, [1, 0xff, 0, 0, 0xff]); } } ```

classification.name: KnownPanicsLint
evidence: implementation: compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/known_panics_lint.rs

analysis.summary: In KnownPanicsLint, union-typed locals must be marked non-const-propagatable before any layout query. The old path called tcx.layout_of for every candidate local, including unions; for a union like InvalidTag containing an enum with an unsupported repr(packed), layout calculation panicked in rustc_abi instead of returning Err, causing ICE #123710. The fix short-circuits ty.is_union() to NoPropagation, avoiding layout entirely because KnownPanicsLint does not const-propagate unions anyway.
analysis.originalLogic: For each local whose can_const_prop entry is still enabled, KnownPanicsLint obtained body.local_decls[local].ty and called tcx.layout_of(param_env.and(ty)). It allowed const propagation when the result was Ok(layout) with layout.size < Size::from_bytes(MAX_ALLOC_LIMIT); otherwise it set *val = ConstPropMode::NoPropagation and continued. Thus there was no union-specific guard before requesting layout.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to run the layout query for union-typed candidate locals before deciding whether they could be const-propagated. That transformation treated layout_of as a safe probe whose failure would simply disable propagation, but for the buggy union layout it panicked: the issue reports an ICE from layout_of_union with the assertion `non-Aggregate field with matching ABI but differing alignment`. The correction is to detect ty.is_union(), set NoPropagation, and never call layout_of for that local.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR bodies processed by KnownPanicsLint, specifically locals whose declared type is a union and that are being considered for const propagation. The motivating regression input contains a union with an enum field, where the enum has #[repr(packed)] plus #[repr(u32)] and the union field is not Copy/ManuallyDrop, producing normal diagnostics E0517 and E0740 but previously also ICE during layout.
analysis.trigger: KnownPanicsLint iterates a local marked as potentially const-propagatable, finds that its type is a union, and the old code calls tcx.layout_of on it. Layout calculation can then hit the union-layout assertion in rustc_abi and panic rather than return an Err, so the existing fallback in the match arm never gets a chance to mark the local non-propagatable.
preconditions: The local is present in cpv.can_const_prop when KnownPanicsLint performs its can-const-prop refinement.
The implementation lacks an early ty.is_union() check and therefore invokes tcx.layout_of for that local.
The union's layout calculation can panic in layout_of_union, for example when a union contains an enum with an unsupported repr such as #[repr(packed)].
pitfalls: Do not rely on layout_of returning Err to reject a local: layout calculation can ICE/panic before producing a Result.
Checking only layout.size against MAX_ALLOC_LIMIT is insufficient because the layout query itself may panic for a union.
The union short-circuit must happen before tcx.layout_of; computing layout first and merely discarding the result does not prevent the ICE.
Union const propagation is intentionally disallowed by KnownPanicsLint, so avoiding the layout query does not lose a supported optimization there.
The regression test is a UI test that still emits E0517 and E0740; absence of an ICE, not a successful compilation, is the relevant outcome.
Do not generalize this fix to every pass or every non-struct type; the historical change is specifically about KnownPanicsLint's treatment of unions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test such as tests/ui/lint/ice-const-prop-unions-known-panics-lint-123710.rs that declares a union whose field is an enum annotated with #[repr(packed)] and #[repr(u32)], then constructs the union. Expected stderr should contain E0517 for the invalid enum repr and E0740 for the non-Copy union field, but no rustc ICE/layout panic. The patch also removes the tests/crashes/123710.rs known-bug test, reflecting that this is now a fixed regression rather than an open crash. No compiler was built or executed here; this testing approach is inferred from the supplied UI test and stderr changes.
